A.explanation: Too small for a $20^{\circ}$ rotation. It does not equal the transmitted component $2.6 \cos 20^{\circ}$ in $\text{cm}$.

B.explanation: This is $2.6 \sin 20^{\circ} \approx 0.89 \text{ cm}$, the component blocked by the filter, not the component transmitted along the $20^{\circ}$ axis.

C.explanation: This is $2.6 \cos^2 20^{\circ} \approx 2.3 \text{ cm}$. The $\cos^2 \theta$ law applies to intensity, while CRO amplitude follows the amplitude $\cos \theta$ law.

D.explanation: Transmitted amplitude is $2.6 \cos 20^{\circ} \approx 2.4 \text{ cm}$, the vertical amplitude resolved along the transmission axis.

hints: Notice the starting CRO amplitude is $2.6 \text{ cm}$ for vertically polarised microwaves and the filter transmission axis is $20^{\circ}$ to the vertical.
Recall that the transmitted wave amplitude is the component of the incident amplitude along the transmission axis, while Malus law $I = I_0 \cos^2 \theta$ describes intensity.
Calculate $2.6 \text{ cm} \times \cos 20^{\circ}$ and check why $\cos^2 20^{\circ}$ and $\sin 20^{\circ}$ would give different CRO amplitudes.
walkthrough: Identify the given information: incident amplitude $A_0 = 2.6 \text{ cm}$ with vertical polarisation, and angle between incident polarisation and transmission axis $\theta = 20^{\circ}$.
State the physical rule: a polarising filter transmits the component of the electric field amplitude along its transmission axis, so $A = A_0 \cos \theta$.
Distinguish from intensity: intensity is proportional to $(\text{amplitude})^2$, so intensity follows $I = I_0 \cos^2 \theta$, but the CRO voltage and trace height follow amplitude.
Evaluate the intermediate result: $\cos 20^{\circ} \approx 0.940$, so $A \approx 2.6 \times 0.940 \text{ cm} \approx 2.44 \text{ cm}$.
Round sensibly to the precision of the options, about $2.4 \text{ cm}$. This is option D.
